summary: Steel lookout tower, 30 m (98 ft), recorded by Alberta as built in 2012 and still marked active; no history beyond the province's layer was found.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower, 30 m (98 ft) tall per the Alberta wildfire lookout layer
facts.status_note: Alberta's wildfire lookout layer marks it active; no source read describes its condition

staffing.status: active per Alberta layer; lookout sites are generally staffed April to October (province-wide statement, not site-specific)

access.note: No public visiting arrangement found. The layer's access mode is fly. Level carried from the brief's record; no source read states a closure.

visit.trail_note: No visitor route described; the layer lists the access mode as fly, which suggests access by air

events.note: Present structure per Alberta's wildfire lookout layer (year of construction). No earlier tower on this site is described in the sources read.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: every fact about this tower comes from the province's wildfire lookout layer, plus two province-wide or general Alberta pages. No history, fire, staffing or condition record for this tower was found in two searches and about four page or query reads. The layer is classed by the province as Protected; the story uses only the year, height, type, access mode and active flag, with no coordinates or map. The layer marks LOCATION_VERIFIED as N, so the mapped position is unconfirmed. Brief record (2012 build, 30 m, standing, closed) matches the layer; no correction. Access level 'closed' is carried from the brief's record; no source read states a closure. 'Fly' is read as access by air, which is an inference. Alberta Historic Places says many current lookouts were rebuilt on the sites of first-generation lookouts, but no source ties that to this tower, so the story does not say it. No photos added; licences were not checked.
